images.filename: Twin railway lift bridges over St. Lawrence Seaway in Montreal.jpg
images.caption: A side-by-side pair of identical vertical-lift bridges in Greater Montreal, Quebec, Canada, carrying a double-track rail line over the St. Lawrence Seaway.  More specifically, the location is in Kahnawake, just across from the city of Montreal proper.  The twin lift bridges over the Seaway are on the same rail line as the Saint-Laurent Railway Bridge, which crosses the St. Lawrence River, and are only about 1,200 feet (370 m) south of that longer bridge.  In the background (to the east) is the southern section of the Mercier Bridge (road bridge on Quebec Route 138).
images.alt: A side-by-side pair of identical vertical-lift bridges in Greater Montreal, Quebec, Canada, carrying a double-track rail line over the St. Lawrence Seaway.  More specifically, the location is in Kahnawake, just across from the city of Montreal proper.  The twin lift bridges over the Seaway are on the same rail line as the Saint-Laurent Railway Bridge, which crosses the St. Lawrence River, and are only about 1,200 feet (370 m) south of that longer bridge. images.filename: HMY Britannia underway in July 1959, with Queen Elizabeth II and Dwight D. Eisenhower.jpg
images.caption: Her Majesty's Yacht Britannia underway in July 1959. The British Queen Elizabeth II and the U.S. president Dwight D. Eisenhower are visible on her brigde. On 20 July 1959, Britannia sailed the newly opened Saint Lawrence Seaway en route to Chicago, Illinois (USA), where she docked, making the Queen the first British monarch to visit the city. President Eisenhower was aboard Britannia for part of this cruise.
images.alt: Her Majesty's Yacht Britannia underway in July 1959. The British Queen Elizabeth II and the U.S. president Dwight D. Eisenhower are visible on her brigde. On 20 July 1959, Britannia sailed the newly opened Saint Lawrence Seaway en route to Chicago, Illinois (USA), where she docked, making the Queen the first British monarch to visit the city.
